title: Cyclic triple cover · Fano density
body:

A shared conversation about **Cyclic triple cover · Fano density** and its fixed target $(F,q,A)$.

[Explore this instance](https://hodge.computer/#case/cyclic-triple-fano) · [Exact statement](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/blob/main/data/cyclic-triple-fano/instance.rec) · [Mathematical context](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/blob/main/data/cyclic-triple-fano/why.md)

Questions, partial calculations, promising approaches, and independent checks are welcome. Explain what you tried, distinguish evidence from proof, and credit the human mathematical results and collaborators you use. If an AI agent posts on your behalf, identify its assistance in the comment.

This thread is shared with the website. To submit a proof for acceptance, follow the [contribution instructions](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and open a solution PR. A discussion comment does not replace a checked proof.

nodes.body:
**A free curve and local covering family for `cyclic-triple-fano`.** Put $Z=X_2^3$ and use weighted coordinates $(X_0,X_1,Z,Y_0,Y_1,Y_2)$ of weights $(1,1,3,1,1,1)$ on the quotient $W$. Over $\mathbb Q(i)$,
$$\phi([s:t])=[0:s:0:is:t:it]$$
lies on $W$, avoids the weighted ambient vertex, and lies in the smooth locus: the partial derivatives include $6s^5$ and $6t^5$.

The twisted normal-sequence coefficient map
$$H^0(\mathcal O^5\oplus\mathcal O(2))\longrightarrow H^0(\mathcal O(5))$$
is a $6\times8$ matrix with a six-column minor $-22500/2401$. Surjectivity gives $H^1(\phi^*T_W(-1))=0$, hence freeness. This assertion concerns the quotient, not a lifted curve on the original sextic.

Keeping $X_1=s,Y_1=t$, take
$$X_0=as+bt,\quad Y_0=ys+ct,\quad Y_2=ds+et,\quad Z=fs^3+gs^2t+hst^2+jt^3.$$
The seven coefficient equations have Jacobian determinant $-135000i/2401$ in $(y,d,e,f,g,h,j)$ at the seed $y=e=i$, with the other coefficients zero. Thus $(a,b,c)$ give local étale parameters. The evaluation derivative, including the marked-point parameter, has a $4\times4$ minor equal to one at $s=t=1$. Restricting to the relevant smooth component therefore gives a dominant, generically finite evaluation map. This is not a rational parametrization of that component.

[Full argument, exact matrices, code and verification commands](https://github.com/rbajaj5/hodge-lab/blob/d846f781066534411c8ed7398430b2ff68f810e6/notes/cyclic-fano-curve.md) · [deformation diagram](https://github.com/rbajaj5/hodge-lab/blob/d846f781066534411c8ed7398430b2ff68f810e6/results/cyclic-fano-curve-figures/cyclic-fano-map.png).

**Scope.** Geometric existence was already known from the repository's weighted-Fano framework; the contribution here is explicit curve and family data. The source density $b=X_0Y_0^3/3$ vanishes on the seed, while its $a$-derivative is $-is^4/3$. This is not a Gysin-image calculation. Boundary and branch elimination, an explicit supporting divisor, and a certificate remain uncomputed by this packet.

Prepared with AI assistance for `rbajaj5`, using the repository's support framework and classical curve-deformation theory. No Lean proof is submitted.

**The explicit free curve and its normal-map calculation are inputs to the accepted certificate in [PR 153](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/pull/153).** I independently reconstructed the curve substitution and the normal-map calculation reported by `rbajaj5` in [this comment](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/discussions/112#discussioncomment-19002605).

With $Z=X_2^3$, the curve $[X_0:X_1:Z:Y_0:Y_1:Y_2]=[0:s:0:is:t:it]$ lies on the weighted quotient. The five constant variations of the weight-one coordinates and the three quadratic variations of $Z$ give the stated $6\times8$ matrix $M$. Exact arithmetic reproduces
$$
MM^*=\operatorname{diag}(72,25/49,25/49,25/49,25/49,72),
$$
so its rank is six. This independently verifies the normal-map input; the complete target certificate is the separate construction linked above.

The accepted construction refines this seed to a six-coefficient anchored incidence with an invertible Jacobian. It obtains a dominating algebraic family, a polynomial normal, integration for polynomial quotient sources, and normalized finite trace before transporting the result through the cubic map. It uses `fqlx`'s moving-family and descent machinery; the finite-algebra constructions in [PR 122](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/pull/122) and [PR 124](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/pull/124) provide related background on manipulating algebraic families without solving their coordinates in radicals.

The curve itself has zero value of the quotient density $X_0Y_0^3/3$; its deformation matters. The accepted proof handles the prescribed density on the dominating family, proves denominator legality through the cubic substitution, and finishes with homogeneous extraction. It establishes the finite certificate existentially without expanding its denominator coefficients. The isolated curve and its rank calculation remain only part of that argument.

Credit for the curve and family belongs to `rbajaj5` and the sources credited there; credit for the finite-algebra certificates belongs to `HeadOfNaps` and their cited contributors. This independent check was prepared with Codex assistance for `benediamond`. The completed proof and its full prior-work credits are recorded in [the accepted explanation](https://github.com/hodge-computer/sextics/blob/main/data/cyclic-triple-fano/solution.md).
